nodes.label: Spec Kit Workflow Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Sequential pipeline: constitution → specify → clarify → plan → tasks + checklist → analyze + implement. Each command produces artifacts consumed by the next. Constitution provides governance constraints. Clarify reduces ambiguity before planning. Analyze validates cross-artifact consistency. Checklist provides requirement-quality gates. Git extension hooks enable auto-commit and branch management at each stage.

nodes.label: Extension Hook System
nodes.rationale: All commands check `.specify/extensions.yml` for hook registration under `hooks.before_<command>` and `hooks.after_<command>` keys. Hooks have optional/mandatory flags and condition expressions. Git extension registers hooks for auto-commit, branch creation, and validation at each pipeline stage. This separates extension concerns from core command logic.

nodes.label: Constitution Framework
nodes.rationale: Template-based governance system using placeholder tokens `[ALL_CAPS]` in `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Defines non-negotiable principles (MUST/SHOULD), governance rules, versioning (semver), and amendment procedures. Acts as the authority during analyze phase - violations are always CRITICAL. All downstream templates (spec, plan, tasks) must stay in sync with constitution changes.

nodes.label: Checklist as Unit Tests for Requirements
nodes.rationale: Checklists test requirement quality (completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, coverage) not implementation correctness. Metaphor: if spec is code in English, checklist is its unit test suite. Items use question format ('Are X defined?') with traceability markers [Spec §X.Y], [Gap], [Ambiguity], [Conflict]. Grouped by quality dimension categories.
